title: Uncertainty Blowup via Algebraically Repetitive Variables (Dependency Problem)
pattern: Evaluating an uncertain interval or measurement metric by referencing the same interval variable multiple times in a single formula.
why_bad: In interval arithmetic, each occurrence of a variable is treated as independent. The "dependency problem" treats $R_1$ in the numerator as having no correlation to $R_1$ in the denominator, which mathematically blows up the reported uncertainty band to be falsely wide.
detection: Look for functions where an interval, error margin, or range struct is passed, and the same variable name is read more than once in an equation.
strength: Strong` — violates interval-mathematics dependency constraints, causing artificial error inflation.
source: Harold Abelson et al. - *Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs* (1996), Section 2.1.4, p. 284.
